![Logistics](assets/art/logo.png) # Logistics: Automation **A modern Minecraft logistics and pipe mod with authentic in-pipe item motion** [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-indemnity83%2Flogistics-blue?logo=github)](https://github.com/indemnity83/logistics) [![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-green.svg)](LICENSE) [![Minecraft](https://img.shields.io/badge/Minecraft-26.1-brightgreen.svg)](https://www.minecraft.net/) [![Fabric](https://img.shields.io/badge/Fabric-0.18.6-orange.svg)](https://fabricmc.net/) [![Discord](https://img.shields.io/badge/Discord-Join-5865F2?logo=discord&logoColor=white)](https://discord.gg/94DP3CVNVt)
## ⚠️ Early Development **Logistics is in active development.** Core pipe transport works, but expect rough edges, missing features, and the occasional bug. Report issues on [GitHub](https://github.com/indemnity83/logistics/issues) if something breaks, or [join the Discord](https://discord.gg/94DP3CVNVt) for help and discussion. ## About Logistics is a Fabric mod inspired by BuildCraft and Logistics Pipes, bringing authentic item pipe systems to modern Minecraft. Items travel smoothly through thin pipes with visible motion, integrating seamlessly with other mods via Fabric's Transfer API. **Design Principles:** - **Material-Based Identity** - Each pipe uses distinct vanilla materials for visual clarity - **Layered Progression** - Three tiers: Mechanical pipes (basic operations), Smart pipes (decisions), Network logistics (abstract services) - **Authentic Visuals** - Items travel continuously through pipes with visible speed - **Mod Interoperability** - Works with any mod using Fabric Transfer API (ItemStorage) - **Classic Ergonomics** - Simple placement, visible connections, easy to understand ## How It Works Logistics is built on a **three-tier system** that grows with your world progression. ### Tier 1: Mechanical Pipes (Implemented) **Basic routing without item awareness** Start here. These pipes perform mechanical operations—moving, merging, extracting, deleting—but they don't look at what's flowing through them. They just do their job, every time, regardless of item type. - **Stone Transport Pipe (Stone)** - Very slow backbone connectivity with random routing - **Copper Transport Pipe (Copper)** - Backbone connectivity with random routing - **Item Extractor Pipe (Wood)** - Pull items from adjacent inventories into your network - **Item Merger Pipe (Iron)** - All inputs converge to a single output - **Golden Transport Pipe (Gold)** - Speed boost when powered by redstone - **Item Passthrough Pipe (Sandstone)** - Connects only to pipes; bypasses inventories - **Item Void Pipe (Obsidian)** - Delete unwanted items ### Tier 2: Smart Pipes (Implemented) **Item-aware routing decisions** These pipes are intelligent. They inspect items and change behavior based on what they see. This is where your network becomes conditional and responsive. - **Item Filter Pipe (Diamond)** - Route specific items to specific destinations (item-aware) - **Item Insertion Pipe (Quartz)** - Prefer inventories with space; otherwise route to pipes ### Tier 3: Network Logistics (Implemented) **System-aware automation and requests** Your inventories become abstract resources. Provider modules advertise what's available; supplier modules push stock; requester modules pull what's needed; crafting pipes handle on-demand autocrafting. **Pipes:** - **Basic Logistics Pipe** - Network backbone; accepts and deposits addressed items with optional filtering - **Provider Logistics Pipe** - Advertises adjacent inventory contents to the network - **Requester Logistics Pipe** - Requests specific items from the network on demand - **Supplier Logistics Pipe** - Keeps a target inventory stocked with configured items - **Crafting Logistics Pipe** - Automates crafting recipes fulfilled by the network - **Process Logistics Pipe** - Routes in-progress crafting jobs to dedicated machines - **Satellite Logistics Pipe** - Remote output point for routing items to distant destinations - **Chassis Pipes (MkI–MkV)** - Modular pipes with swappable logistics module slots **Modules (for Chassis Pipes):** - **Provider Module (I–II)** - Advertise inventory contents at different range/speed tiers - **Extractor Module (I–III)** - Pull items from adjacent inventories at increasing speeds - **Passive / Active Supplier Module** - Push stock to requesters (passive waits; active seeks) - **Crafter Module (I–III)** - Fulfill crafting requests at increasing speeds - **Quicksort Module** - Route items by type to sorted destinations - **Terminus Module** - Mark a pipe as a terminal endpoint; prevents routing past it - **Sink Module** - Accept any overflow items - **Polymorphic Sink Module** - Accept overflow, treating NBT-equal items as equivalent - **Enchantment Sink Module** - Accept overflow, ignoring enchantment differences - **Mod Sink Module** - Accept overflow filtered by mod origin Each tier builds on the previous one—you'll use all three together as your base grows. ## Features Logistics includes a complete system for item transport, power generation, and automation. ### Pipes Transport items through networks with different behaviors: - **Basic Transport** - Stone and Copper pipes for backbone connectivity - **Extraction & Routing** - Wood (extractor), Iron (merger), Diamond (filter), Quartz (insertion) pipes - **Special Pipes** - Gold (speed boost), Sandstone (passthrough), Obsidian (void) [View all pipes →](https://indemnity83.github.io/logistics/pipes/) ### Power RF energy generation and distribution: - **Redstone Engine** - Simple, safe, steady power; never overheats - **Stirling Engine** - Fuel-powered with heat management; shuts down safely on overheat - **Creative Engine** - Infinite power for testing and creative mode - **Power Cables (Copper/Gold/Ender)** - Distribute energy from engines to connected machines at increasing transfer rates [Learn about power systems →](https://indemnity83.github.io/logistics/power/) ### Automation - **[Macerator](https://indemnity83.github.io/logistics/automation/macerator/)** - Grind ores, gems, and materials into fine dusts for smelting and crafting - **[Kiln](https://indemnity83.github.io/logistics/automation/kiln/)** - Electric furnace; smelts any vanilla smelting recipe using RF energy - **[Laser Quarry](https://indemnity83.github.io/logistics/automation/laser-quarry/)** - Automated 16×16 mining with energy-scaled speed ### Tools - **[Wrench](https://indemnity83.github.io/logistics/tools/wrench/)** - Configuration tool for pipes and machines - **[Marking Fluid](https://indemnity83.github.io/logistics/tools/marking-fluid/)** - Color-code your pipe networks ## Installation **Requirements:** Minecraft 26.1+ • Fabric Loader 0.18.6+ • Fabric API • Java 25+ **Download from:** - [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/indemnity83/logistics/releases) (includes dev builds) - [Modrinth](https://modrinth.com/mod/logistics) (stable releases) - [CurseForge](https://www.curseforge.com/minecraft/mc-mods/logistics-automation) (stable releases) [Full installation guide →](https://indemnity83.github.io/logistics/getting-started/install/) ## Quick Start 1. **Craft pipes** - Start with stone or copper transport pipes 2. **Connect to inventories** - Pipes automatically connect to chests and other storage 3. **Extract items** - Use wood extractor pipes (wrench to configure) 4. **Route and filter** - Combine different pipe types to build your network [Build your first pipe network →](https://indemnity83.github.io/logistics/getting-started/first-network/) ## Status ### ✅ Implemented - Thin pipe blocks with 6-way connections - Server-side traveling item simulation with continuous progress - Client-side smooth visual rendering - Extraction from and insertion into adjacent inventories - Mechanical and Smart pipe behaviors - Network logistics: provider, requester, supplier, crafting, satellite, and chassis pipes - Autocrafting via vanilla Crafter integration - Redstone, Stirling, and Creative engines with heat management - Power cables (copper, gold, ender) for RF energy distribution between machines - Macerator for grinding ores, gems, and materials into dusts - Kiln as an RF-powered electric furnace for any vanilla smelting recipe - Laser Quarry with automatic frame construction and energy-scaled mining speed ### 🚧 In Progress - NeoForge mod loader support (architecture groundwork complete; SPI implementations in progress) ### 🔮 Future - Fluid pipes with Transfer API integration - Power/cost system for logistics operations - Additional pipe upgrades and advanced logistics features See the [documentation](https://indemnity83.github.io/logistics/) for detailed information on pipes, power, automation, and more. ## Contributing Contributions welcome! Report issues on [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/indemnity83/logistics/issues). For code contributions, see `CLAUDE.md` for development guidance. ## License This project is licensed under the MIT License - see the [LICENSE](LICENSE) file for details. Some textures are licensed under CC BY 4.0 or CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 - see [CREDITS.md](CREDITS.md) for attribution details. ## Acknowledgments Inspired by: - **BuildCraft** — Classic pipe mechanics and visual style - **Logistics Pipes** — Request/provider logistics system design - **Forestry** — machines and progressive automation - The Fabric community for excellent modding tools and APIs **Textures:** - Some textures used, adapted, or inspired from [Unused Textures](https://github.com/malcolmriley/unused-textures) by Malcolm Riley, licensed under [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/) - Some textures used, adapted, or inspired from [TextureRepository](https://github.com/Futureazoo/TextureRepository) by Futureazoo, licensed under [CC BY-NC-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-sa/4.0/)
[Report an Issue](https://github.com/indemnity83/logistics/issues) • [Documentation](https://indemnity83.github.io/logistics/) • [Discord](https://discord.gg/94DP3CVNVt)

<details>
<summary>📝 Walkthrough</summary>

## Walkthrough

This PR fixes five pre-existing bugs in the laser quarry system. The `outputItem` method now conditionally returns based on whether transport insertion succeeds, allowing rejected items to fall through to inventory and drop fallbacks. The `insertIntoSlot` method now triggers container change notifications when inserting into empty slots and when merging into matching stacks. Energy consumption state is snapshotted before clearing to prevent the LED indicator from staying lit after the quarry finishes. The phase runner now fully resets to the clearing phase when custom bounds are set, and the clearing-to-frame-building transition is centralized with proper client synchronization.

## Possibly related issues

- [`#407`: Laser quarry: items lost when forceInsert into pipe above returns false](https://github.com/Indemnity83/logistics/issues/407) – Addressed by the conditional return in `outputItem` that only returns early on successful transport insertion.
- [`#408`: Laser quarry: insertIntoSlot does not call setChanged() on target container](https://github.com/Indemnity83/logistics/issues/408) – Addressed by adding `setChanged()` calls after both empty-slot and merge mutations, verified by new tests.
- [`#409`: Laser quarry: consumedEnergyThisTick can stay true after the quarry finishes](https://github.com/Indemnity83/logistics/issues/409) – Addressed by snapshotting consumption state before the finish check and syncing clients conditionally.
- [`#410`: Laser quarry: CLEARING → BUILDING_FRAME transition not immediately synced to clients](https://github.com/Indemnity83/logistics/issues/410) – Addressed by centralizing the phase transition in `transitionFromClearingToBuildingFrame()` which calls both `setChanged()` and `syncToClients()`.
- [`#411`: Laser quarry: setCustomBounds doesn't reset frameBuildIndex or phase](https://github.com/Indemnity83/logistics/issues/411) – Addressed by fully reinitializing phase, frame index, and break progress in `onCustomBoundsSet()`.
- [`#423`: Laser quarry: clearing scan can pass null target to shouldSkip](https://github.com/Indemnity83/logistics/issues/423) – Addressed by adding an explicit null check after the scan loop that triggers the phase transition helper before using the target.

## Possibly related PRs

- [Indemnity83/logistics#99](https://github.com/Indemnity83/logistics/pull/99): Both PRs modify LaserQuarry energy-consumption/tick-sync behavior (`LaserQuarryBlockEntity.tick` and `consumedEnergyThisTick`/LED working state handling).
- [Indemnity83/logistics#406](https://github.com/Indemnity83/logistics/pull/406): Refactors quarry phase logic into `QuarryPhaseRunner`; this PR fixes state management and synchronization bugs in the refactored phase runner and energy tracking.

This PR hardens energy storage operations across the logistics system by defensively validating and clamping invalid inputs. Core components (`EnergyComponent`, `LogisticsConfig.QuarryConfig`) and platform-specific adapters (Fabric, NeoForge) now reject non-positive transfer amounts with early returns, clamp negative capacities to zero, and ensure non-finite multiplier values produce zero instead of propagating through calculations.   else

    CapacitySupplier-->>EnergyComponent: capacity
    EnergyComponent->>EnergyComponent: clamp capacity -> non-negative
    EnergyComponent->>EnergyComponent: compute room, toInsert
    EnergyComponent->>Caller: return toInsert
  end

  Caller->>EnergyComponent: extract(maxAmount)
  alt maxAmount <= 0
    EnergyComponent->>Caller: return 0
  else
    EnergyComponent->>EnergyComponent: clamp maxExtract and amount -> non-negative

  end

<details>
<summary>📝 Walkthrough</summary>

## Walkthrough

This PR adds a common ClientModelRegistry (register/find/all, ModelKey, Provider SPI, registerProvider/get) and FabricModelLoader to bridge the registry into Fabric's model-loading pipeline. Client MODEL statics in Automation, Power, and Pipe modules are migrated to register ResourceId-backed ClientModelRegistry.ModelKey constants and expose MODEL.init() called from client init. Renderers (LaserQuarry, Marker, Pipe, Engine) now resolve baked BlockStateModel instances via ClientModelRegistry.get(ModelKey). The legacy ModelKeyRegistry class is removed.

## Sequence Diagram(s)

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant Client as CLIENT (MODEL statics)
  participant Registry as ClientModelRegistry
  participant Loader as FabricModelLoader
  participant Plugin as ModelLoadingPlugin
  participant ModelManager as Fabric ModelManager

  Client->>Registry: register(ResourceId)  (class-load)
  Client->>Loader: FabricModelLoader.setup() (client init)
  Loader->>Registry: all() -> build ExtraModelKey mapping
  Loader->>Plugin: register unbaked extra models (pre-bake)
  Plugin->>ModelManager: inject unbaked entries
  ModelManager-->>Loader: baked models available later
  ModelManager->>Registry: provider.get(ModelKey) at render-time
  Registry-->>Renderer: BlockStateModel or null
```

## Walkthrough

The PR adds multi-loader support (Fabric and NeoForge) across CI and Gradle. GitHub Actions workflows (build-pr, build-prerelease, build-release, build-snapshot) use a loader matrix and set Gradle tasks to `:${LOADER}:jar`; artifact paths and uploads are loader-specific and publishing steps are gated to Fabric. The root build depends on `:fabric:build` and `:neoforge:build`. `gradle.properties` and `settings.gradle` receive NeoForge config/plugin values, a runnable `neoforge/build.gradle` is added, and a NeoForge mod entrypoint `LogisticsNeoForge` is implemented.

<details>
<summary>📝 Walkthrough</summary>

## Walkthrough

This PR adds a power cable subsystem: new CableBlock/CableBlockEntity types and three CableTier variants (COPPER, GOLD, ENDER) registered in LogisticsPower. It implements CableNetwork and CableNetworkManager to discover connected cable graphs, route and distribute RF energy each tick without buffering in cables, and perform transactional transfers constrained by per-cable transfer rates. A new EnergyDemandProvider interface is introduced and implemented by LaserQuarryBlockEntity, MaceratorBlockEntity, and CreativeSinkBlockEntity to expose per-tick demand; cable entities query devices for demand when allocating and routing energy. README and blockstate assets for the new cables were also added.

## Sequence Diagram(s)

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Client as Player/Client
    participant Source as Energy Source (Engine/Machine)
    participant Cable as CableBlock / CableBlockEntity
    participant Manager as CableNetworkManager
    participant Network as CableNetwork
    participant Router as Route Finder
    participant Target as Target Device (with EnergyDemandProvider)
    participant Tx as TransactionContext

    Source->>Cable: insert(amount, side)
    Cable->>Manager: insert(level, pos, side, amount, tx)
    Manager->>Manager: ensure networks built for level
    Manager->>Network: delegate insertion to containing network
    Network->>Network: collectDeviceConnections()
    Network->>Target: query EnergyDemand (networkDemandPerTick or storage headroom)
    Network->>Network: alloc

payload.author: Indemnity83
payload.body:
Restructured the branch for the multiloader layout introduced in #318/#320. No logic changes — just moved files to the right places and fixed one bug that surfaced during compilation.

**File moves:**
- `src/main/java/...` → `common/src/main/java/...`
- `src/client/java/...` → `fabric/src/client/java/...`
- `src/gametest/java/...` → `fabric/src/gametest/java/...`
- `src/test/java/...` → `common/src/test/java/...`
- `src/main/resources/...` → `common/src/main/resources/...`

**Fabric API extraction:** `LogisticsPower` had Fabric-specific calls (`ServerTickEvents`, `ServerWorldEvents`, `ItemGroupEvents`) that can't live in common code. Moved those into `LogisticsFabric`.

**Bug fix:** `CreativeSinkBlockEntity` was missing its `EnergyDemandProvider` implementation (`networkDemandPerTick()`) and the transaction-aware `pendingInserts` tracking. The game tests were calling `sink.networkDemandPerTick()` so this was a compilation error. Ported the full implementation from the PR.

Build passes including game tests. Let me know if anything looks off.

This pull request implements state key-based module targeting for supplier modules. When a wrench is used on a supplier module, its state key is now captured and passed through the GUI handler chain (`SupplierScreenHandler` and `SupplyInventory`). `PipeModuleHelper` is extended with new overloaded methods that accept an optional state key parameter to support precise module lookup by both class type and state key. This enables the GUI to target a specific supplier module instance rather than resolving to the first matching module on the pipe. Tests verify the state key matching logic.

sequenceDiagram
    actor Player
    participant SupplierModule
    participant PipeModuleHelper
    participant SupplierScreenHandler
    participant SupplyInventory

## Walkthrough

This PR updates the logistics block-entity persistence API to thread a `HolderLookup.Provider registries` parameter through `BaseBlockEntity` persistence hooks (`saveLogisticsData`, `loadLogisticsData`, `loadLegacyData`) and all overridden implementations in several block entities (Kiln, LaserQuarry, Marker, engines, Macerator, Pipe, CreativeSink, etc.). Inventory and item (de)serialization now use the provided `registries` (via `registries.createSerializationContext(NbtOps.INSTANCE)`) instead of calling `level.registryAccess()`. Final save/load entry points and legacy-migration paths are adjusted to pass the provider. A new unit test verifies persistence works without a `level`.

## Sequence Diagram(s)

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant BlockEntity as BlockEntity (subclass)
    participant Base as BaseBlockEntity
    participant Registries as HolderLookup.Provider
    participant NBT as CompoundTag / RegistryOps

    BlockEntity->>Base: saveLogisticsData(tag, registries)
    Base->>Registries: createSerializationContext(NbtOps.INSTANCE)
    Registries->>NBT: provide RegistryOps
    Base->>NBT: serialize inventories/items using RegistryOps
    Base-->>BlockEntity: return (tag written)

    BlockEntity->>Base: loadLogisticsData(tag, registries)
    Base->>Registries: createSerializationContext(NbtOps.INSTANCE)
    Registries->>NBT: provide RegistryOps
    Base->>NBT: deserialize inventories/items using RegistryOps
    Base-->>BlockEntity: state restored
```

<details>
<summary>📝 Walkthrough</summary>

## Walkthrough

The ProcessModule replaces a single persistent "active job" with a durable FIFO queue of per-dispatch entries. `isActive()` reflects queue non-emptiness. `onDispatch()` always appends a queue entry (subject to `MAX_QUEUE_SIZE`) that snapshots requester position, optional delivery UUID, executions, initial extraction counters, pending input orders, and output config. `collectOutputs` processes only the head entry, validating requester and snapshot, canceling/removing invalid entries, advancing per-entry extraction bookkeeping, routing deliveries using the head entry's delivery UUID, and removing entries when fulfilled. `onDetach()` cancels all queued input orders and clears the queue. Supply is always advertised; dispatch caps produced amount.

## Sequence Diagram(s)

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Dispatcher
    participant Queue
    participant Extractor
    participant Delivery
    participant Requester

    Dispatcher->>Queue: append ENTRY (requesterPos, deliveryUUID?, executions, extr_0=0, extr_req, pendingInputOrders, outputSnapshot)
    Note right of Queue: durable FIFO of per-dispatch entries
    Extractor->>Queue: peek head ENTRY(0)
    Queue-->>Extractor: ENTRY(0) or empty
    alt ENTRY(0) missing/invalid requester or outputSnapshot
        Extractor->>Queue: cancel pendingInputOrders for ENTRY(0)
        Extractor->>Queue: remove ENTRY(0)
    else ENTRY(0) valid
        Extractor->>Extractor: extract items using outputSnapshot, increment extr_0
        alt extr_0 >= executions * outputCount (extr_req)
            Extractor->>Delivery: route extracted items to deliveryUUID from ENTRY(0)
            Delivery->>Requester: deliver items to requesterPos
            Extractor->>Queue: remove ENTRY(0)
        end
    end
```

</details>

<!-- walkthrough_end -->

<details>
<summary>📝 Walkthrough</summary>

## Walkthrough

This change introduces a command-based architecture for network operations. Three new types are added: CommandResult to represent execution outcomes, NetworkCommand (a sealed interface) with three concrete implementations (ExtractCommand, InsertCrafterInputsCommand, DeliverCommand) to encapsulate network actions, and NetworkCommandExecutor to bridge domain logic with world interactions. PipeNetwork is updated to use this new command pattern instead of directly calling worldView, improving separation of concerns between domain and world-coupled code.

## Sequence Diagram

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant PN as PipeNetwork
    participant NCE as NetworkCommandExecutor
    participant WV as IWorldView
    participant CR as CommandResult

    PN->>PN: Create ExtractCommand
    PN->>NCE: execute(ExtractCommand)
    activate NCE
    NCE->>WV: dispatch(provider, requester, item, amount)
    activate WV
    WV-->>NCE: shipped (long)
    deactivate WV
    
    alt shipped > 0
        NCE->>CR: ok(shipped)
        CR-->>NCE: CommandResult
    else shipped == 0
        NCE->>CR: failed()
        CR-->>NCE: CommandResult
    end
    
    NCE-->>PN: CommandResult
    deactivate NCE
    
    PN->>PN: result.isSuccess()?
    
    alt isSuccess
        PN->>PN: Log and record itemsHandled
    else !isSuccess
        PN->>PN: Mark provider unavailable
    end

<details>
<summary>📝 Walkthrough</summary>

## Walkthrough

This pull request introduces periodic reconciliation to the JobCoordinator, enabling detection and recovery from supply loss during job execution. The implementation adds a tick method to JobCoordinator that runs at regular intervals, checks active jobs for unmet demand, and triggers replanning when loss is detected. Supporting changes include a new ReconciliationService for loss detection, a ReconciliationResult record for expressing loss amounts, a bidirectional job-to-order mapping structure, and a NetworkController query method to verify order existence. The reconciliation flow is integrated into the main PipeNetwork tick loop.

## Sequence Diagram(s)

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant PN as PipeNetwork
    participant JC as JobCoordinator
    participant RS as ReconciliationService
    participant NC as NetworkController
    participant RP as RequestPlanner

    PN->>JC: tick(controller)
    activate JC
    JC->>JC: Check if tick interval reached
    alt Interval reached
        JC->>JC: Iterate active jobs with pending orders
        JC->>RS: reconcile(job, view)
        activate RS
        RS->>RP: Plan with PARTIAL fulfillment
        RS-->>JC: ReconciliationResult(amountLost)
        deactivate RS
        alt Loss detected
            JC->>RS: replan(job, missingAmount, view)
            activate RS
            RS->>RP: Generate new FulfillmentPlan
            RS-->>JC: Optional<FulfillmentPlan>
            deactivate RS
            alt Replan successful
                JC->>NC: hasOrder(staleOrderId)
                NC-->>JC: true/false
                JC->>JC: Cancel stale order
                JC->>JC: Place new order
                JC->>JC: Update jobToOrder and orderToJob
                JC->>JC: Toggle job state: REPLANNING → ACTIVE
            else Replan failed
                JC->>JC: Record invalidation and log
            end
        else No loss
            JC->>JC: Continue to next job
        end
        JC->>JC: Reset reconciliation counter
    end
    deactivate JC
```

</details>

## Walkthrough

The pull request introduces a reservation system to explicitly track item allocations in the logistics network. It adds four new types: AllocationState (enum with states PLANNED, RESERVED, EXTRACTING, IN_TRANSIT, DELIVERED, INVALIDATED), ItemReservation (data class holding reservation details), ReservationId (type-safe record), and ReservationManager (manager class with lifecycle operations). NetworkController is modified to integrate ReservationManager, calculating effective available stock by subtracting active reservations from raw supply, creating reservations during dispatch with state transitions at key lifecycle events (cancellation, delivery, provider unavailability).

## Sequence Diagram

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant NC as NetworkController
    participant RM as ReservationManager
    participant R as ItemReservation
    participant AS as AllocationState

    NC->>RM: reserve(orderId, provider, requester, item, amount, hard)
    RM->>R: new ItemReservation(id, ..., PLANNED)
    RM->>RM: Store in reservations map
    RM-->>NC: Return ReservationId

    NC->>RM: effectiveAvailable(provider, item, raw)
    RM->>RM: Filter active reservations
    RM-->>NC: Return raw - activeAmount

    NC->>RM: transition(resId, IN_TRANSIT)
    RM->>R: Update state field
    R-->>RM: State updated to IN_TRANSIT

    NC->>RM: markDelivered(requester, item)
    RM->>RM: Find IN_TRANSIT reservation
    RM->>R: Update state to DELIVERED
    RM->>RM: Remove from reservations

    alt On Cancellation
        NC->>RM: releaseByOrder(orderId)
        RM->>R: Release reservation
        RM->>RM: Remove from map
    end

    alt Provider Unavailable
        NC->>RM: invalidateByProvider(provider)
        RM->>R: Update state to INVALIDATED
        RM->>RM: Mark as inactive
    end
```

## Walkthrough

This pull request introduces a fulfillment mode system to the logistics network. A new FulfillmentMode enum distinguishes between PARTIAL (dispatch available items) and FULL (dispatch only when full amount available) fulfillment strategies. The SupplierModule's order placement logic is refactored to use a SupplierModeConfig-based decision model instead of direct mode branching. For window-bounded modes, available space and pending items are computed to determine order size. For non-window-bounded modes, trigger-met checks validate whether restocking is needed, with fulfillment mode determining whether availability is required before ordering. The Order record, ILogisticsNetwork interface, NetworkController, and PipeNetwork are updated to carry and propagate fulfillment mode information throughout the order placement and dispatch pipeline. Dispatch logic is guarded to prevent partial fulfillment when fulfillment mode is FULL.

- **Indemnity83/logistics#180**: Modifies SupplierModule ordering logic for pending items and mode-based request calculations, closely aligned with this PR's config-driven ordering refactor.
- **Indemnity83/logistics#176**: Modifies NetworkController's order placement and dispatch logic, related to how orders are processed and handled in the network.
